$comment: T2.9/T3.2 (PLAN-ci-time-budget, operator spec W). Measured cost per lane, read by
scripts/ci-runner/lanes.ts's shardPlan (its optional 4th argument) so a sharded lane
balances legs by real duration once one exists, instead of by scheduler `weight`.
'jobs' is each job's fixed cost (p90 minutes, setup through the first runner step);
'units' is each shard-plan unit id's own p90 in MILLISECONDS, keyed exactly as the
id appears in gates.lock.json (a quality-code check id) or in a test lane's own
SEEDED 2026-09-26 with 'concurrency' only (operator ruling D-W1: stay on GitHub Free,
20 concurrent jobs) -- 'jobs' and 'units' are empty until T3.2's
'budget_report.py --refresh' runs against real green CI data. An empty 'units' means
every shardPlan caller falls back to `weight` for every unit, so quality-code's plan
is unaffected until this file actually names one of its ids (see the selftest control
'shardPlan(durations: {}) is byte-identical to shardPlan() with no durations argument'
T3.1's freshness check (not yet built) reds when 'refreshed_at' is older than 14 days.
